## Index

### Findings

- [`RWF-001`](findings/RWF-001.md): RWF-001 — UMD-style `module.exports` assignment via a locally-aliased variable is never recognized

- [`AUD-12`](findings/AUD-12.md): AUD-12 — An all-UNKNOWN scan exits 0, identical to a clean scan, with no machine-readable signal that nothing was decided
- [`AUD-13`](findings/AUD-13.md): AUD-13 — Babel-style `__esModule` interop is not modeled for a default ESM import of a CommonJS module
- [`AUD-14`](findings/AUD-14.md): AUD-14 — An OSV record's `withdrawn` field is not parsed; a withdrawn advisory is still analyzed
- [`AUD-15`](findings/AUD-15.md): AUD-15 — An UNKNOWN's reason text falsely claims a package "was never traversed" when the true cause is that no rule names it
- [`AUD-16`](findings/AUD-16.md): AUD-16 — Two README sentences and two HTML-report sentences describe cache/no-finding behavior that AUD-05/06/07/08/09 show is false
- [`PRM-12`](findings/PRM-12.md): PRM-12 — A call/`new` whose callee resolves to a Node builtin, but which receives a function-valued argument, emits no edge
- [`PRM-13`](findings/PRM-13.md): PRM-13 — VT-213's inline-callback rescue displaces the unresolved edge for an otherwise-unattributable callee instead of adding to it
- [`PRM-14`](findings/PRM-14.md): PRM-14 — Loose equality (`==`/`!=`) is evaluated as if it were strict, pruning a branch real Node does not prune
- [`PRM-15`](findings/PRM-15.md): PRM-15 — A same-file `const require = ...` shadow is matched by identifier text before the lexical authority runs
- [`PRM-16`](findings/PRM-16.md): PRM-16 — A same-file caller is treated as the unique call site of an exported higher-order parameter, even with cross-file callers
- [`PRM-17`](findings/PRM-17.md): PRM-17 — A higher-order parameter's reassignment inside the function body is never checked before its call sites are treated as authoritative
- [`PRM-18`](findings/PRM-18.md): PRM-18 — The TypeScript checker's static apparent type of a receiver is used as the runtime receiver, even when reassigned
- [`PRM-19`](findings/PRM-19.md): PRM-19 — A derived class's synthesized implicit default constructor gets no edge to the resolved base constructor
- [`PRM-20`](findings/PRM-20.md): PRM-20 — `bindCallee` resolves a trailing method chain (`x.y()`) to the receiver `x` itself, discarding which method was called
- [`PRM-21`](findings/PRM-21.md): PRM-21 — A same-file `const` binding shadows an ambient global (`require`, `eval`, `process`, `module`) for the whole file
- [`PRM-22`](findings/PRM-22.md): PRM-22 — The loader classifier's alias lookup for module/eval/vm-style capabilities is first-match and scope-blind
- [`PRM-23`](findings/PRM-23.md): PRM-23 — A truncated module-load closure (`traversal_truncated`) does not block families B/C, missing a closure-widening hook outside the truncated file set
- [`PRM-24`](findings/PRM-24.md): PRM-24 — A builtin loader that starts new execution (`cluster.fork`/`setupPrimary`) is not classified as a loader
- [`PRM-25`](findings/PRM-25.md): PRM-25 — A configured `{file, symbol}` entrypoint is matched by node-name text; an unmatched symbol still reports the entrypoint root complete
- [`PRM-26`](findings/PRM-26.md): PRM-26 — Export-to-function mapping takes the first same-named match in file-scan order, not the declaration the export site binds to
- [`PRM-27`](findings/PRM-27.md): PRM-27 — A later string-key or getter property in an object-literal export is ignored; the earlier plain-key value is still published
- [`PRM-28`](findings/PRM-28.md): PRM-28 — A computed export key (`[K]: danger`) is resolved against a same-file `const` binding chosen scope-blind
- [`PRM-29`](findings/PRM-29.md): PRM-29 — A property write inside a called `configure()` function is not seen as competing with the export map
- [`PRM-30`](findings/PRM-30.md): PRM-30 — A `module.exports = {...}` literal unpacking wins over a later `module.exports.run = danger` member write
- [`PRM-31`](findings/PRM-31.md): PRM-31 — Root-requirement materialization matches a candidate node by AST name text, so a same-named decoy elsewhere satisfies it
- [`PRM-32`](findings/PRM-32.md): PRM-32 — `this.X = ...` at module scope and an aliased `const api = module.exports; api.run = ...` are invisible to root-requirement detection
- [`PRM-33`](findings/PRM-33.md): PRM-33 — Under `module: commonjs`, TypeScript's node10 module resolution is used at runtime and ignores the package's `exports` map
- [`PRM-34`](findings/PRM-34.md): PRM-34 — A `file:`-vendored dependency whose real npm lockfile entry has no `name` is silently dropped entirely
- [`PRM-35`](findings/PRM-35.md): PRM-35 — A cache-directory write failure (`ENOTDIR`) aborts the whole scan with exit 4 instead of degrading to a diagnostic
- [`PRM-36`](findings/PRM-36.md): PRM-36 — The `--cve` unreported-candidate reason "no advisory was discovered for any sibling instance" is computed from the filtered result, not the true discovery set
- [`PRM-37`](findings/PRM-37.md): PRM-37 — A tagged-template call (`` tag`x` ``) gets no call-graph edge at all
- [`PRM-38`](findings/PRM-38.md): PRM-38 — Implicit protocol invocations (`toString`/`valueOf` coercion, thenable resolution, `Symbol.iterator`) invoke user code with no call-graph edge
- [`PRM-60`](findings/PRM-60.md): PRM-60 — `unsupported_*` reasons are treated as never widening the closure, but four capability-receiver shapes let them load a new module
- [`PRM-61`](findings/PRM-61.md): PRM-61 — Export forwarding resolves to the first "own" binding of a name, which a later `module.exports` replacement or property write can make stale
- [`PRM-62`](findings/PRM-62.md): PRM-62 — An ESM `let`-bound export reassigned after its declaration is attributed to its stale initial value
- [`PRM-63`](findings/PRM-63.md): PRM-63 — Several ways of replacing/mutating `module.exports` (bracket member write, module-alias write, `Object.assign(module.exports, …)`) are not recognized as export writes
- [`PRM-64`](findings/PRM-64.md): PRM-64 — A versionless package instance is evaluated only against advisories its own (missing) version would filter to
- [`PRM-65`](findings/PRM-65.md): PRM-65 — The real `OsvProvider` sends one request with no `page_token`, so a paginated OSV response's later pages are silently never seen
- [`PRM-66`](findings/PRM-66.md): PRM-66 — A workspace member with a malformed manifest is silently skipped only when its lockfile entry is versionless
- [`PRM-67`](findings/PRM-67.md): PRM-67 — `SUPPORTED_MODEL_EXCLUSIONS` omits `--conditions` and `--import`/preload flags, so the model's stated scope is false
- [`PRM-101`](findings/PRM-101.md): PRM-101 — Site B hands a phantom target to reachability with no closure corroboration, certifying export-*-only code unreachable although its top level runs
- [`PRM-102`](findings/PRM-102.md): PRM-102 — Site A/B selection is keyed by advisory package NAME, not by exact `PackageInstance`
- [`PRM-103`](findings/PRM-103.md): PRM-103 — A cyclic `require` observes an intermediate `module.exports` value mid-cycle, but last-write-wins attribution only considers the final write
- [`PRM-104`](findings/PRM-104.md): PRM-104 — A `FunctionDeclaration` binding used as an export has no reassignment check, unlike the class/function-expression branches next to it
- [`PRM-105`](findings/PRM-105.md): PRM-105 — Member access and call results are treated as opaque in the escape sweep, hiding a capability reached through `[x][0]`, `.at(0)`, a computed key or `Reflect.get`
- [`PRM-106`](findings/PRM-106.md): PRM-106 — `require.bind(...)` is deliberately excluded from the capability-receiver check
- [`PRM-107`](findings/PRM-107.md): PRM-107 — `module.paths` is recognized only through a small, fully-enumerated set of literal method-name calls
- [`PRM-108`](findings/PRM-108.md): PRM-108 — A destructured builtin binding's imported name falls back to the local name for a string-literal or computed property key
- [`PRM-109`](findings/PRM-109.md): PRM-109 — `graph.ts` restates the same "`unsupported_*` reasons cannot introduce a new module" premise PRM-60 disproves
- [`PRM-110`](findings/PRM-110.md): PRM-110 — The HTML report's per-finding summary reads only the first `unknownReasons` entry, so a rule mismatch reads as "no reason recorded"
- [`PRM-111`](findings/PRM-111.md): PRM-111 — An empty `--cve` value (`--cve ""`) is accepted and silently returns zero findings rather than being rejected
- [`PRM-112`](findings/PRM-112.md): PRM-112 — `instanceof` against a class defining a static `[Symbol.hasInstance]` invokes it with no call-graph edge
- [`PRM-113`](findings/PRM-113.md): PRM-113 — `for await…of` over a value with an async iterator (`[Symbol.asyncIterator]`) invokes it with no call-graph edge
- [`PRM-114`](findings/PRM-114.md): PRM-114 — Assigning a function to `Error.prepareStackTrace` registers a callable hook invoked with no call-graph edge
- [`PRM-115`](findings/PRM-115.md): PRM-115 — TypeScript decorators (legacy and standard) are call expressions at class-definition time with no modeled edge
- [`PRM-116`](findings/PRM-116.md): PRM-116 — A JSX element is a call to its configured factory with no modeled edge
- [`PRM-117`](findings/PRM-117.md): PRM-117 — An object's `[util.inspect.custom]()` method, run by `console.log` / `util.inspect` / `util.format("%o")`, gets no call-graph edge
- [`PRM-118`](findings/PRM-118.md): PRM-118 — A getter or setter body is attributed to the enclosing owner, so an accessor real Node never runs yields a fabricated `AFFECTED` path
